purpose: Reconcile collected evidence with E3/E5 and Longevity/Transparency decisions, without installing target software.

git.role: Individual custodian of a local repository
git.configuration: Installed Git; synthetic tracked history, branch, annotated unsigned tag, stash, ignore rules, local configuration and one submodule. Global/system configuration and executable hooks are disabled by the runner.
git.backup_contract: Full main/submodule bundles plus separate local configuration. Reconstruct after original paths become unavailable; compare all refs, history metadata, tracked file bytes, config, submodule commit and fsck.
git.consequential_operations: Preview and execute a tracked-history reset, recover its committed tip using reflog, inspect clean -n, then explicitly force deletion on a disposable copy and recover the untracked file from a separate backup.
git.departures: No LFS, executable hooks, signed-tag authenticity, hosted permissions, network isolation, remotes or corruption injection. These were not silently satisfied: the earlier broader candidate scenario remains open and judgments are limited to this configured local core workflow.

sqlite.profile: Embedded relational-engine profile: schema, rows, types, keys, relationships, view and trigger definitions; not the application-specific meaning of arbitrary databases
sqlite.role: Developer/custodian using Python's installed SQLite API, explicit transactions, foreign_keys ON and trace callback ON
sqlite.recovery: Repeat the previously recorded dump/backup evidence and inspect schema/rows/view/foreign keys; confirm a restored trigger actually executes.
sqlite.consequential_operations: Rollback a DELETE, rollback to a savepoint, observe a rejected foreign-key write, rollback a DROP TABLE, commit an authorized change and reopen it; record SQL trace.
sqlite.departures: Not a GUI or arbitrary client, not the newest upstream revision, not another SQLite implementation, not a filesystem/crash/corruption stress test. Audit/authorization is supplied at this API boundary, not automatically enforced on every client.

other_applications: Source/fixture evidence already retained is reviewed as evidence, not reported as runtime success. Incomplete requirement coverage stays Not Verified and does not justify a positive principle finding.
schema_repair: Invalid requirement values become not_verified unless an individually justified decision establishes pass/fail. No automatic partial-to-pass or meets-to-pass rule.
